description: This bar chart, from the paper “How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media,” illustrates the average number of likes for posts categorized by their similarity to the most similar group of posts, with the x-axis labeled “Most similar group of posts” and displaying five distinct intervals: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450]. The y-axis, labeled “Avg. Like #”, is scaled linearly from 400 to 600 in increments of 50, with tick marks and labels at each 50-unit interval. Each of the five light blue bars represents one of these similarity intervals, and all bars are of approximately equal height, with the bar for the (0,90] interval reaching an average of 600 likes, the bar for the (90,180] interval at approximately 565 likes, the bar for the (180,270] interval at approximately 565 likes, the bar for the (270,360] interval at approximately 595 likes, and the bar for the (360,450] interval at approximately 585 likes. Each bar is accompanied by a vertical error bar extending above and below its top, indicating variability in the average like count for that group. The bars are arranged in the order of increasing similarity interval, from left to right, and are not sorted by height. There are no visual distinctions such as shading, bolding, or annotations to emphasize any particular bar.
